transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-05-27
- Start: 15:30 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Rivera (Redwood SE), Olivia Park (Redwood SE), Aisha Hassan (Voltica Head of Search), Tom Groves (Voltica CTO), Rina Patel (Voltica ML Eng), Marco Liu (Voltica SRE)

Summary:
Voltica is evaluating embedding + rerank architecture for their customer support search and knowledge layer. Primary concerns: tail latency at peak (with bursty traffic from support tickets), data residency/VPC controls, and a graceful fallback when vector DB or primary reranker is overloaded. They want to understand trade-offs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments for a mixed hybrid-search strategy (ann + rerank).

Topics covered:
- Integration patterns with vector DBs (fanout to MMR/ANN vs single-stage rerank)
- Embedding dimensionality and quantization impact on throughput and recall
- Fallback and circuit-breaker strategies when VDB is slow
- Security requirements (KMS, SSO, SOC2) and network options (VPC peering vs private deploy)
- Bench plan for throughput verification and cost estimation

Action items (also in metadata):
- Send security pack (SOC2 + ISO) and private deployment checklist
- Schedule bench test and share test datasets
- Voltica to provide sample queries and SLA targets

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Maya, AE on the account, with Diego and Olivia from our SE team. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Aisha (Voltica): doing good, thanks. we wanted to go deeper on embeddings + rerank today, specifically how to keep search stable during spikes.
[00:18] Tom (Voltica): yeah our support volume has these 2–3 hour spikes after releases, so p99 latency matters more than averages.
[00:27] Diego (Redwood): absolutely — and thanks for the context. can you share current numbers? qps, index size, dimensions?
[00:35] Rina (Voltica): sure, roughly 3M docs in the KB, average embedding dim today 384 (we're experimenting with 768 for quality), and baseline qps around 20 with burst to 120 for 10–30 minutes. target p99 for search+rerank is ~350ms ideally.
[00:55] Olivia (Redwood): ok that's helpful. two levers we usually look at: where to run the nearest-neighbor (ANN) vs where to run rerank. most folks do ANN at VDB (managed) and run a lightweight rerank locally in the inference tier, but there are hybrid approaches.
[01:12] Marco (Voltica): when the VDB slows down we get cascading timeouts and then the web UI falls back to a simple keyword search that is garbage. we want a safer fallback, maybe cached prefixes or a cheaper model.
[01:25] Maya (Redwood): yes — we recommend a fallback playbook: prioritize cached results for top queries, run a smaller/quantized embed + cheap reranker for tail, and degrade gracefully to keyword only if all else fails. we can show config examples.
[01:39] Tom (Voltica): ok, curious on cost — if we move some work to Dedicated how different is the unit cost vs Hosted?
[01:47] Diego (Redwood): ballpark: Hosted is easiest to start and competitive per-token, Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and better per-request economics at sustained high qps, while Private (VPC/on-prem) adds fixed infra and ops cost but gives you control for residency and network egress. we can run numbers once you share a 24h sample load.
[02:07] Rina (Voltica): on embeddings size — do we need to switch to 768 or 1024? our experiments showed marginal recall lift after 512 for our domain.
[02:17] Diego (Redwood): depends on dataset. dimensionality impacts index size and ANN latency. you can also quantize (8-bit, 4-bit or PQ) to reduce footprint. for reranking, the large model matters more; many customers do 512 embeddings + a MLM-style reranker on top.
[02:33] Aisha (Voltica): do you see any vendors doing 128 dims successfully?
[02:36] Olivia (Redwood): yes but usually with domain-specific training and careful similarity function tuning. 128 is aggressive; it's great for throughput but risks recall loss.
[02:45] Tom (Voltica): so what's the recommended architecture for Voltica's constraints — 3M docs, 120 burst, p99 350ms?
[02:54] Diego (Redwood): a pattern we like:
  1) ANN search in a sharded VDB with a hot cache for top N queries
  2) First-stage filter with 512-d embeddings quantized to 8-bit for footprint
  3) Lightweight on-the-fly rerank with a 2–4 layer transformer or a distilled cross-encoder on Dedicated hosts for critical paths
  4) Fallback: lower-cost reranker (smaller model) or cached results; circuit-breaker to prevent cascading timeouts

[03:33] Marco (Voltica): and network — if we choose Hosted, can we still have a VPC peering or private connections?
[03:39] Maya (Redwood): Hosted currently supports private peering in regions and IP allowlists; for strict network controls we usually recommend Dedicated or Private which can be deployed in your VPC with customer-managed routing and KMS.
[03:52] Tom (Voltica): audit logs and KMS — how deep do audit logs go? we have compliance needs.
[03:58] Olivia (Redwood): we provide request-level audit logs, model-version mapping, and KMS integration for key material in Private or Dedicated. Hosted has envelope encryption and SOC2 controls; Private brings you HSM/KMS in your cloud account.
[04:12] Aisha (Voltica): can you clarify what you mean by "model-version mapping"?
[04:15] Diego (Redwood): basically, we record which model and which quantization profile served each request — useful for debugging regressions and for audits. sometimes those labels get munged in the transcript, ha.
[04:24] (laughter)

[04:30] Rina (Voltica): bench plan — what's typical? we want a smoke test that simulates bursts and measures tail latency on both Hosted and Dedicated.
[04:39] Diego (Redwood): we run 24h job with ramping bursts, include cold-cache and warm-cache phases, and vary fanout. we'll need your sample queries and corpus; Diego: we typically shard the VDB 8–16 ways for you size.
[04:54] Tom (Voltica): what's 'fanout' in your terms?
[04:57] Olivia (Redwood): fanout = how many shards or replica sets we query in parallel — higher fanout increases recall but adds tail risk. some teams do adaptive fanout where we query fewer shards and then expand on low-confidence results.
[05:12] Maya (Redwood): important tradeoff: if you push for max recall (full fanout) at 120 qps, you might exceed your latency SLO unless you provision Dedicated capacity. adaptive fanout with early-stopping and rerank often hits a good balance.

[05:35] Marco (Voltica): do you have examples or configs for circuit-breakers? we want to avoid thundering herd on a slow VDB.
[05:42] Diego (Redwood): yes — simple rules: set per-shard timeouts, an overall query timeout, and a queue depth limit; then use a token-based circuit-breaker that reduces fanout or switches to cached responses when error rates climb. we can share our playbook doc (link).
[05:58] Maya (Redwood): we just uploaded a short playbook to the shared folder — link: https://redwood.ai/embed-playbooks/voltica-initial (note: internal link)

[06:05] Aisha (Voltica): for Private deployment, how long is the onboarding typically?
[06:09] Olivia (Redwood): Private deployments vary but plan 6–8 weeks for on-prem or air-gapped, 3–4 weeks for VPC-hosted with our automation. Dedicated is often 2–3 weeks. Hosted is immediate.

[06:23] Tom (Voltica): what about retry semantics — do you recommend client-side retries on top of Redwood routing?
[06:29] Diego (Redwood): yes, but keep retries idempotent and limited — exponential backoff and circuit-breaker signals are better. excessive client retries can worsen tail latency.

[06:40] Rina (Voltica): question about quantization: if we go 8-bit quant for embeddings, what about accuracy drift?
[06:45] Diego (Redwood): small accuracy loss is common but many workloads see minimal impact with per-dataset calibrations and PQ tweaks. we'll run an eval with your dataset to measure recall delta.

[06:58] Aisha (Voltica): any concerns about vendor lock-in if we put heavy logic into Redwood-specific routing?
[07:03] Maya (Redwood): we try to keep the abstractions portable — you can pin model versions and export configs. also we recommend keeping a lightweight transformer locally as a fallback; not everything should be proprietary.

[07:18] Tom (Voltica): does Redwood support hybrid search where we combine exact keyword filtering with ANN prefilter?
[07:24] Olivia (Redwood): yes — hybrid pipelines are common: apply an SQL or inverted-index filter first, then ANN on the filtered set. that reduces fanout cost and can boost precision.

[07:40] Marco (Voltica): during spikes, would you recommend debounce on user input or server-side throttling?
[07:45] Diego (Redwood): both — debounce on the client helps a lot; server-side rate limits and fair-queueing keep noisy clients from stomping the system.

[07:58] Aisha (Voltica): security again — SSO and RBAC: can we map Redwood roles to our IdP groups?
[08:03] Olivia (Redwood): yes, SAML/SCIM integration available for Dedicated and Private; Hosted supports SSO for account access but group-sync for RBAC is richer on Dedicated/Private.

[08:18] Rina (Voltica): latency targets — if we provision Dedicated for rerank, what's realistic p99 for cross-encoder on small model?
[08:26] Diego (Redwood): depends on model size and batch settings. a distilled cross-encoder on a Dedicated host can hit sub-200ms p99 for 10–50 qps per host; you scale horizontally for higher qps. caching top replies also greatly reduces load.

[08:48] Tom (Voltica): how do you manage KV cache across replicas? we saw inconsistencies in other systems.
[08:55] Olivia (Redwood): Redwood has a coordinated KV cache with sticky routing to reduce miss amplification; we also expose cache-control hints so you can pin hot prefixes. sometimes transcripts show KV as 'KV cash' in the auto text, heh.
[09:10] (laughter)

[09:18] Maya (Redwood): okay, let's walk through a concrete fallback scenario: shard slowdown => drop to adaptive fanout => use quantized embedding + smaller reranker => if still failing, return cached top-k. any questions?
[09:33] Aisha (Voltica): what about correctness — if we use smaller reranker, how do we know it isn't returning hallucinations?
[09:40] Diego (Redwood): the smaller reranker should be calibrated and have confidence scores; low confidence triggers client messaging and optionally escalate to human-in-the-loop. we also run synthetic evals to measure hallucination risk.

[09:55] Rina (Voltica): can Redwood do A/B comparisons between, say, 512 vs 768 dims in a live pilot?
[09:59] Maya (Redwood): yes, we can do traffic split rollouts and record per-route metrics. Redwood Console will show token/cost breakdown and model-level quality deltas if you provide evaluation prompts.

[10:12] Tom (Voltica): about costs — can you ballpark Dedicated infra costs for our profile?
[10:17] Diego (Redwood): rough estimate: to sustain 120 qps with low tail we might suggest 6–8 Dedicated GPU hosts for the rerank tier plus dedicated CPU nodes for ANN gateway. final pricing depends on model choices and reserved capacity discounts. we'll produce a detailed TCO after the bench run.

[10:38] Aisha (Voltica): competition: we've looked at Pinecone for the VDB and Milvus for self-host; how do you integrate with those?
[10:45] Olivia (Redwood): Redwood can point to any vector store via adapters — we have connectors for Pinecone, Milvus, FAISS-backed endpoints; the integration pattern is the same: Redwood handles routing and rerank, the VDB is queried as first-stage.

[10:58] Marco (Voltica): any known issues with Pinecone at high fanout?
[11:02] Diego (Redwood): some customers reported increased variance at very high fanout; that's why adaptive fanout and per-shard timeouts are important.

[11:12] Rina (Voltica): what telemetry will we get during the bench?
[11:15] Maya (Redwood): per-request latency, per-shard latency, cache hit rates, model version used, token counts, error rates, and a heatmap of query types. we'll upload a benchmark sheet (gsheet) with all metrics.

[11:27] Aisha (Voltica): perfect. about data residency — is the Hosted instance in our preferred region?
[11:32] Olivia (Redwood): we have regions in NA and EU; if you need APAC residency we can explore Private or a dedicated region.

[11:42] Tom (Voltica): for the bench test, we want to include a simulated release day spike pattern. can Redwood synthesize that?
[11:48] Diego (Redwood): yes we can replay a release-day traffic profile; provide historical traces if you have them or we can construct a synthetic pattern based on qps burst numbers.

[12:00] (background cross talk, "hold on, I'll share the dataset")

[12:10] Rina (Voltica): i'm going to upload a 10k query sample and a 50k doc slice to the shared folder after this call.
[12:16] Maya (Redwood): great — thanks. we'll need the labelset for recall calculations if you have it.

[12:22] Aisha (Voltica): one last question — can Redwood do partial rerank on top-k retrieved candidates only, to save cost?
[12:28] Olivia (Redwood): absolutely, that's the common approach: retrieve top 100 by ANN, rerank top 10 with a heavier model. you can tune both thresholds.

[12:40] Tom (Voltica): what should we expect for a POC timeline if we want both Hosted and Dedicated comparisons?
[12:46] Diego (Redwood): we can run a hosted bench in 1–2 days after you send data; Dedicated bench requires provisioning (2–3 weeks) but we can mimic Dedicated characteristics on Hosted for an initial head-to-head. full POC typically 4–6 weeks.

[13:05] Maya (Redwood): ok wrapping up — recap and next steps: 1) Maya will send security pack & deployment checklist; 2) Diego will propose bench windows and test plan; 3) Rina will upload dataset + SLA targets; 4) we'll schedule a 30-min follow-up to lock dates.

[13:25] Aisha (Voltica): sounds good. thanks everyone.
[13:29] Tom (Voltica): thanks.

[13:32] (meeting ends)
